{{Short description|Function studied in real analysis}}
A '''Baire one star function''' is a type of [[function (mathematics)|function]] studied in [[real analysis]]. A function <math>f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}</math> is in class Baire* one, written <math>f \in \mathbf{B}^{*}_{1}</math>, and is called a Baire one star function if, for each [[perfect set]] <math>P \in \mathbb{R}</math>, there is an [[open interval]] <math>I \in \mathbb{R}</math>, such that <math>P \cap I</math> is nonempty, and the restriction <math>f |_{P \cap I}</math> is [[continuous function|continuous]]. The notion seems to have originated with B. Kirchheim in an article titled 'Baire one star functions' (Real Anal. Exch. 18 (1992/93), 385–399).
The terminology is actually due to Richard O'Malley,  'Baire* 1, Darboux functions' Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 60 (1976), 187–192.  The concept itself (under a different name) goes back at least to 1951. See H. W. Ellis, 'Darboux properties and applications to nonabsolutely convergent integrals' Canad. Math. J., 3 (1951), 471–484, where the same concept is labelled as [CG] (for generalized continuity).
